The '''2026 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election''' took place on 7 May 2026, as part of the [[2026 United Kingdom local elections]]. All 45 members of [[Tower Hamlets London Borough Council]] were elected, with the [[2026 Tower Hamlets mayoral election]] taking place at the same time to determine the council's leader. The election took place alongside the [[2026 London local elections|local elections in the other London boroughs]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Coughlan |first=Joe |date=2025-04-30 |title=London local elections, why they aren't in 2025 and when the next ones will be |url=https://www.mylondon.news/news/uk-world-news/london-local-elections-arent-any-31429137 |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=My London |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Local authority, combined authority, and county combined authority election cycles in England |url=https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/election-timetable-in-england/election-timetable-in-england |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=GOV.UK |language=en}}</ref> [[Aspire (political party)|Aspire]] won 33 out of the 45 seats up for election, gaining majority control of the council.

==Background==
[[File:Tower Hamlets UK local election 2022 map.svg|thumb|Result of the 2022 council election]]
The thirty-two [[London boroughs]] were established in 1965 by the [[London Government Act 1963]]. They are the principal authorities in Greater London and have responsibilities including education, housing, planning, highways, social services, libraries, recreation, waste, environmental health and revenue collection. Some powers are shared with the [[Greater London Authority]], which also manages passenger transport, police, and fire.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The essential guide to London local government {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/essential-guide-london-local-government|access-date=2021-10-10|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>

Since its formation, Tower Hamlets had generally been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control. The [[SDP–Liberal Alliance]] won a majority of seats in the [[1986 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|1986 election]], and the newly formed [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] won a majority in the [[1990 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|1990 election]]. There was also a period of [[no overall control]] from 2014 to 2018. From 1990 to 2006, all councillors elected to the council were Labour or Liberal Democrats. In the [[2006 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|2006 election]], Labour maintained its majority by winning 26 seats, but the new [[Respect Party]] won twelve seats, with the Conservatives on seven and the Liberal Democrats on six.<ref>{{cite web |last=Manning |first=Luke |title=The battle for Tower Hamlets |url=http://www.theguardian.com/politics/2006/may/05/localelections2006.localgovernment |website=The Guardian |date=5 May 2006 |access-date=22 October 2021}}</ref> In the [[2010 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|2010 election]] Respect lost all but one of its seats, with Labour winning 41, the Conservatives winning eight and the Liberal Democrats winning one. Respect was the only party to advocate a change in executive arrangements at the council by the introduction of a directly elected [[mayor of Tower Hamlets]]. A mayoral petition was successfully arranged by the Respect activist Abjol Miah, which was successful.<ref name=SunTel>{{cite web |last=Gilligan |first=Andrew |title=Tower Hamlets extremist vote poses Ed Miliband's first big election test |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/law-and-order/8068839/PICS-AND-PUBLISH-Tower-Hamlets-extremist-vote-poses-Eds-first-big-election-test.html |url-status=dead |work=The Sunday Telegraph |date=17 October 2010 |access-date=18 October 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101018183949/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/uknews/law-and-order/8068839/PICS-AND-PUBLISH-Tower-Hamlets-extremist-vote-poses-Eds-first-big-election-test.html |archive-date=18 October 2010}}</ref>

The Labour councillor [[Lutfur Rahman (British politician)|Lutfur Rahman]], who had been leader of the council from 2008 until he was replaced in 2010 after a [[Channel 4]] documentary linked him to the [[Islamic Forum of Europe]], was selected as his party's candidate for the mayoralty in 2010.<ref name="islamists-crushed">{{cite web |last=Gilligan |first=Andrew |author-link=Andrew Gilligan |title=Islamists are crushed in Tower Hamlets |url=http://blogs.telegraph.co.uk/news/andrewgilligan/100039244/islamists-are-crushed-in-tower-hamlets/ |url-status=dead |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=11 May 2010 |access-date=21 September 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100513210126/http://blogs.telegraph.co.uk/news/andrewgilligan/100039244/islamists-are-crushed-in-tower-hamlets/ |archive-date=13 May 2010}}</ref> He was removed as the candidate by the [[National Executive Committee of the Labour Party]] after "very serious allegations" about the selection.<ref>{{cite web|date=2010-09-21|title=Tower Hamlets: Lutfur's Rahman removed as Labour mayoral candidate in Tower Hamlets |url=http://www.theguardian.com/uk/davehillblog/2010/sep/21/lutfur-rahman-removed-as-labour-tower-hamlets-mayoral-candidate|access-date=2021-10-22|website=The Guardian}}</ref> He subsequently ran as an [[independent politician|independent candidate]] with support from Respect.<ref>{{cite web|date=2010-09-23|title=Rahman to stand as independent in Tower Hamlets mayoral race|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/rahman-to-stand-as-independent-in-tower-hamlets-mayoral-race-3413572|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=2010-10-12|title=Tower Hamlets: interview with independent candidate Lutfur Rahman|url=http://www.theguardian.com/politics/davehillblog/2010/oct/11/tower-hamlets-independent-mayoral-candidate-lutfur-rahman-interviewed|access-date=2021-10-22|website=The Guardian}}</ref> Rahman was elected in the October 2010 election with more than half of the vote in the first round.<ref>{{cite news|date=2010-10-22|title=Lutfur Rahman wins Tower Hamlets mayoral election|language=en-GB|publisher=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-london-11604108|access-date=2021-10-22}}</ref> Rahman established a new political party called [[Tower Hamlets First]] in 2013. He ran for re-election as the Tower Hamlets First candidate in 2014, being re-elected in the second round against the Labour candidate [[John Biggs (London politician)|John Biggs]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Tower Hamlets Mayor Lutfur Rahman re-elected|url=https://www.itv.com/news/update/2014-05-24/tower-hamlets-mayor-lutfur-rahman-re-elected/|access-date=2021-10-22|website=ITV News}}</ref> In the [[2014 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|concurrent council election]], Tower Hamlets First won 18 seats, with Labour on 22 and the Conservatives on 5, resulting in [[no overall control]] of the council.<ref>{{cite web|date=2014-05-22|title=Election results by party, 22 May 2014|url=https://democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk/mgElectionResults.aspx?ID=22&RPID=0|access-date=2021-10-22|website=democracy.towerhamlets.gov.uk}}</ref>

In 2015, Rahman was removed from office and his election was declared void after he was found guilty of electoral fraud. Rahman?|url=https://www.onlondon.co.uk/tower-hamlets-return-of-lutfur-rahman/|access-date=2021-10-22|website=OnLondon|language=en-GB}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{cite news|date=2015-04-23|title=Tower Khan formed the breakaway group the [[People's Alliance of Tower Hamlets]] (PATH) with some other Tower Hamlets Independent Group councillors, which was formally registered in 2018.<ref>{{cite web|last=Brooke|first=Mike|date=2018-02-28|title=Electoral Commission gives People's Alliance of Tower Hamlets recognition as a political party for council election|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/electoral-commission-gives-people-s-alliance-of-tower-hamlets-recognition-3588320|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref> The remaining Tower Hamlets Independent Group councillors formed the new party [[Aspire (political party)|Aspire]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Brooke|first=Mike|date=2018-02-28|title=Labour facing 2nd Tower Hamlets opposition group now recognised by Electoral Commission as 'Aspire' party|url=https://www.eastlondonadvertiser.co.uk/news/local-council/labour-facing-2nd-tower-hamlets-opposition-group-now-recognised-by-3587840|access-date=2021-10-22|website=East London Advertiser|language=en-GB}}</ref>

In the [[2018 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|2018 council election]], Labour won 42 seats with 46.1% of the vote, while the Conservatives won two seats with 9.9% of the vote across the borough. Khan was elected as a councillor for PATH, with her party winning 11.3% of the vote across the borough. Aspire lost all their representation, winning no seats with 15.4% of the vote. The Liberal Democrats received 8.6% of the vote and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] received 7.9% of the vote, but neither won any seats.<ref>{{cite web|last=Grafton-Green|first=Chloe Chaplain, Patrick|date=2018-05-05|title=The full list of results for London's local elections|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/news/politics/london-local-election-results-2018-the-full-list-of-outcomes-for-councils-across-the-capital-a3831926.html|access-date=2021-10-22|website=www.standard.co.uk}}</ref>

In the [[2022 Tower Hamlets London Borough Council election|2022 elections]], Aspire regained control of the council from Labour, winning 24 seats, and also won the [[mayoralty]] with Lutfur Rahman returning as mayor. Reduced to 19 seats, this is the lowest ever number of seats Labour have ever held in the history of Tower Hamlets; the Conservatives retained one seat, while the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] gained one seat.

==Electoral process==
Tower Hamlets, like other London borough councils, elects all of its councillors at once every four years. The previous election took place in 2022. The election took place by multi-member [[first-past-the-post voting]], with each ward being represented by two or three councillors. Electors had as many votes as there are councillors to be elected in their ward, with the top two or three being elected.

All [[Elections in the United Kingdom#Registration procedure|registered electors]] ([[British citizen|British]], [[Irish citizen|Irish]], [[Commonwealth citizen|Commonwealth]] and [[European Union]] citizens) living in London aged 18 or over were entitled to vote in the election. People who live at two addresses in different councils, such as university students with different term-time and holiday addresses, were entitled to be registered for and vote in elections in both local authorities.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=How the elections work {{!}} London Councils|url=https://www.londoncouncils.gov.uk/who-runs-london/london-elections/how-elections-work|access-date=2021-09-14|website=www.londoncouncils.gov.uk}}</ref>
